To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) synthetic fossil liquids can induce skin cancer in C3H mice; (2) the carcinogenic potency of synthetic fossil liquids is less than that of benzo(a)-pyrene, but greater than that of natural fossil liquids; (3) the carcinogenic activity in skin of synthetic fossil liquids appears to reside in the PNA fraction; (4) the PNA fraction from synthetic petroleums is carcinogenic in mouse skin.
the synthetic petroleumes tested were capable of inducing skin tumors in mouse skin and were more potent skin carcinogens than benzo(a) pyrene.
synthetic petroleum liquids are capable of inducing skin tumors in mice, and that the carcinogenic activity is due to the PNA content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the carcinogenic constituents of crude petroleum.
the identification, isolation, and characterization of the carcinogenic components of synthetic and natural petroles, and the determination of the relative potency of the carcinogenic agents present.
the carcinogenic activity and potency of synthetic petroleum fractions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthetic petroleum samples tested are carcinogenic to the skin of C3H mice.
the synthetic petroleumes tested were capable of inducing skin tumors in mice and that the carcinogenic activity could be attributed to the PNA content of these materials.
synthetic petroleums, like benzo(a) pyrene, can induce skin cancer in mice and that, under the conditions of this study, the carcinogenic activity is related to the total PNA content of the crude.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carcinogenic activity in synthetic petroleums appears to be related to the total PNA content, but the carcinogenic activity cannot be attributed to any one PNA compound.
the carcinogenic potency of the synthetic petroleuins evaluated in this study is directly proportional to the total PNA content and is approximately equivalent to 1/500 the potency of benz(a)pyrene.
the carcinogenic potency of a crude synthetic petroleum is related to the carcinogenic potency, per unit of PNA content, of the PNA fraction isolated from that petroleum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carcinogenic potency of the crude synthetic petroleums is due primarily to their PNA content.
synthetic petroleum is not a carcinogen.
synthetic petroleums can be carcinogenic to the mouse skin and that this activity is due to the presence of PNA compounds.
